---
title: "Reproducibility"
---

## Benchmark lifecycle

```text
local targets pipeline
→ reviewed compact outputs
→ promotion validation
→ frozen reference capsule
→ Quarto report
→ GitHub Pages publication
```

Run a local study with compatible input:

```r
Sys.setenv(SBLR_BENCH_STUDY = "01_finemapping")
targets::tar_make()
```

`results/local/` contains ignored working outputs and full local study results. `results/reference/` contains reviewed, versioned, compact benchmark capsules.

Promote reviewed outputs with:

```r
source("scripts/promote_reference_results.R")
```

The promotion validator checks benchmark identity, dimensions, methods, statuses, metrics, finite values, coverage identifiers, and absence of absolute user paths. It refuses to overwrite a snapshot unless `SBLRBENCH_OVERWRITE_REFERENCE=true`.

Each capsule contains compact summaries and metrics, a frozen configuration, exact run command, worked example or smoke test as appropriate, source-code inventory, software versions, checksums and explicit limitations. Capsules may describe public, private, synthetic, downloadable, or non-redistributable sources without assuming every study has genotype data.

For Study 01, the simulated PLINK inputs are publicly accessible from a pinned qgdata commit. `download_sblrbench_example_data()` retrieves and checksum-validates them automatically. The capsule records the pinned URLs, file sizes and MD5 checksums; the large genotype files themselves are not copied into this repository or website.

Public reports exclude sparse-LD files, full posterior samples, full fit objects and `_targets/` stores.

## Prediction benchmark

```r
Sys.setenv(SBLR_BENCH_STUDY = "02_prediction", SBLR_BENCH_REPLICATES = "10")
targets::tar_make()
```

Study 02 uses one deterministic split for every architecture, replicate and active ST method. Allele frequencies and scaling parameters come from training rows; sparse LD and summary statistics also use training rows only. Test phenotypes never enter fitting.

The prediction workflow has four distinct artifacts: `scripts/worked_prediction_example.R` for users, `scripts/prediction_contract_smoke_test.R` for fast contract validation, `scripts/run_prediction_benchmark.R` for the full paired ST study, and a reference capsule created only after review from a clean Git commit. Multi-trait prediction, parameter-estimation and convergence benchmarks remain separate planned work.
